text: Two studies dissect transcriptional control of cancer. Reverse-engineering TLX1/TLX3 oncogenic networks in T cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL) identified them as master regulators of an oncogenic circuit; network analysis pinpointed RUNX1 as a key mediator and predicted its tumor-suppressor role, confirmed by recurrent somatic loss-of-function RUNX1 mutations in human T-ALL. Separately, CDX2 knockdown in colon cancer cells promoted proliferation in vitro, accelerated tumor formation in vivo, and drove G0/G1-to-S transition; overexpression inhibited proliferation. CDX2 knockdown increased, overexpression decreased Wnt/β-catenin activity and targets (β-catenin, cyclin D1, c-myc). XAV-939 suppressed knockdown-enhanced proliferation; CHIR-99021 enhanced inhibition. CDX2 transcriptionally activates GSK-3β and Axin2 by binding the GSK-3β promoter and Axin2 upstream enhancer, suppressing Wnt/β-catenin signaling to inhibit colon cancer growth.
